- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for 5–10 days to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 3-day rolling average of sentiment to weight forecast adjustments.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in 2024 Q2; apply +1.5% bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
